design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (prescription_renewal_handling, category rx). Resumed round 1 after a cut-off with nothing on disk.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. The move (prerequisite) takes 4 factors, the replacement (root) takes 5.

[Why a good test] The patient asks only for her stolen mail-order losartan to be replaced. The agent must (1) read in the replacement policy that its days' supply is fixed only after the prescription stands at a retail pharmacy, (2) see in the prescription record that it stands at Heartland Mail Order Pharmacy, (3) work out from the move policy that the patient's own move is the one write that brings that state about, compute the retail fill length (a 4-allowance minimum over payer class, 12-month dispensing history, authorization span and in-person visit recency) and hand the move to the patient, and only then (4) compute the replacement on the post-move world (lost supply by a dispensing-age method with a payer early-refill share, credit of the remaining fill at the new per-fill length, repeat-loss share, follow-up trim). Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling the fill ledger and two other product lines (billing class, appointments), and ordering two writes; there are only two task tools and they do different things.

[Scope / headroom] Occupied before: nothing (task 0). Claimed: rx_ext_retail_move_fill_days (rx_pharmacy_changed, user tool move_prescription_pharmacy_221e1a97) and rx_ext_replacement_fill_days (rx_fills_authorized/replacement, agent tool authorize_replacement_fill_7c6c01e8). Left for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [5,5]): the controlled-substance agreement signature (rx_compliance_updated, the patient's own act by base rule) and the renewal approval from hold (rx_renewed). Controlled classes allow no bridge, replacement or protocol renewal, so the agreement can only pair with the renewal; the only other patient-owned write in rx is the pharmacy move ('A patient may move the remaining fills of a prescription to another pharmacy'), which is why this task pairs the move with the replacement. Bridge supply and hold writes carry no scored quantity pairable here and stay unclaimed as base capability (M=2).

[Problem-tree card] root rx_ext_replacement_fill_days <- rx_ext_retail_move_fill_days. Edge: kind value_input, gate binding fill_days (F('days_supply')), form state. Prerequisite sentence (replacement rule, affirmative): "A replacement fill's days' supply is fixed only after the prescription stands at a retail pharmacy rather than at a mail-order pharmacy." Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (the pharmacy the prescription stands at, shown by the prescription lookup); no tool, id or code token; strength 'only after', scope exactly the pharmacy kind. Exactly one write of this difficulty changes prescriptions.pharmacy_name: the move. Derivation: sentence + record (pharmacy_name = Heartland Mail Order Pharmacy) + move policy ('A prescription the patient moves to a retail pharmacy is dispensed there in fills of ...' / the retail fill length is recorded at the move) -> the patient's move to a retail pharmacy, handed over at that point. condition: pharmacy_name names a retail pharmacy rather than a mail-order pharmacy (round 2: the days_supply change is the edge's effect, not part of its condition). False at opening: initial_state.prescriptions.546f17fd.pharmacy_name = Heartland Mail Order Pharmacy, .days_supply = 90, .transfer_count = 0. Owner of the resolving tool: user. Topological order: move (step 8) -> replacement (step 10). Deletion sensitivity (sens run): skipping the move gives days_supply_per_fill 0 instead of 21 (credit 90 instead of 34) and leaves the prescription row unchanged. user_scenario never names a pharmacy move (see no_user_hint). Tools validate nothing (see tools_do_not_block).

[Factor card - move, rx_ext_retail_move_fill_days, result 34 = MN of four allowances; baseline paragraph = retail standard 30 days]
- payer_retail_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty billing): ladder Medicaid MC 34 / Medicare Advantage or Part B 60 / Commercial PPO/POS or HMO/EPO 90 / otherwise 30. Evidence billing_accounts 9d6e82df variant 'Medicaid Managed Care Account' -> 34. Baseline figure 30.
- dispensing_adherence_allowance (parameter, history): days dispensed in 12 calendar months >=330 -> 90, 270-329 -> 60, else 30. Evidence: 5 dispensings of 90 days (2025-09-02 .. 2026-08-26) = 450 -> 90. Near-miss: the 2025-07-19 replacement dispensing (13 months back) is outside the window. Baseline figure 30.
- authorization_span_allowance (method): fills remain and, at the per-fill supply the prescription carries, would run past expiry -> days to expiry split evenly among them (fit to the authorization); fills remain and end on or before expiry -> the fill length as written; none -> 30. Evidence refills_remaining 1 x 90 days = 90 <= 182 days to expiration 2027-03-01 -> 90. Baseline figure 30.
- visit_recency_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty appointment): latest completed in-person visit <=183 days -> 90, 184-365 -> 60, else 30. Evidence appointment 6047b080 completed 2025-10-20 (315 days). Near-miss: telehealth bb09d7d6 completed 2026-05-12 is virtual and excluded. Baseline figure 30.
Fall-back (all baselines) 30 != 34.

[Factor card - replacement, rx_ext_replacement_fill_days, result 21; baseline paragraph = one regular fill (per-fill days' supply) = 34 on this world]
- lost_supply_count (method): dispensing age <=14 days -> days until next regular fill due (ceil(days x share) - elapsed); 15-60 -> days left on that dispensing; else one regular fill. Evidence 2026-08-26, 90 days, 5 days back -> ceil(76.5) - 5 = 72. Baseline figure 0.
- payer_early_refill_share (parameter, cross-difficulty billing): Medicaid 85 / Medicare 80 / Commercial 70 / otherwise class 75. -> 85. Baseline figure 14.
- standing_fill_credit (method): fills remain and expiry beyond one per-fill length -> fills x per-fill days; fills remain but expiry within -> min(days to expiry, per-fill days); none -> 0. -> 1 x 34 = 34. Baseline figure 47.
- repeat_loss_share (parameter, multi-source: earlier replacement in 24 months AND missed visits in 12 months): 75 / 50 / 100. Evidence rx_events replacement authorization 2025-07-18 (13 months), no internal_medicine no-show in 12 months (no-show 2025-06-10 is 14 months back: near-miss) -> 75. Baseline figure 31.
- followup_trim (parameter, multi-source cross-difficulty appointment: last in-person visit > 270 days AND booked/confirmed visit): 21 / 7 / 0. Evidence 315 days, booked ef8c9a71 on 2026-10-13 -> 7. Baseline figure 28.
Fall-back 34 != 21. result = MX(0, int((72 - 34) x 75/100) - 7) = 21.

[Base-invariant card] Move: rx_pharmacy_transfer.transferable_status 'The prescription status is active or renewal_requested when the pharmacy is changed.' -> prescriptions.546f17fd.status = active at frozen_time. Standard Maintenance transfer_allowed true, one_time_transfer_only false (transfer_count 0 anyway). Overwrite declared: base clause 'the prescription keeps its fills and expiration and only the pharmacy changes' replaced by the move policy's sentence that fills and expiration are kept and the per-fill days' supply becomes the retail fill length. Replacement: rx_fill_authorization.authorize_when_active 'Fills are authorized only while the prescription status is active.' -> active (the move does not change status). rx_lost_stolen_replacement (no structured gate): class allows replacement, 1 per rolling 12 months; the earlier replacement 2025-07-18 lies outside 2025-08-31..2026-08-31; no police report needed for the class; not controlled. No time eligibility applies to either write (temporal_feasibility []).

[Business-object card] Target: prescription 546f17fd (losartan 50 mg tablet, internal_medicine, Dr. Colin Varga, DO). The stolen object is the 2026-08-26 mail-order dispensing (the latest rx_fill_dispensed row of 546f17fd). Rows in aggregates: 546f17fd dispensings for the 12-month sum and latest dispensing; replacement authorizations of 546f17fd within 24 months (one). Excluded: atorvastatin e8cff9e9 and its three dispensings (other prescription, not in the package), the 2025-03-12 / 2025-06-06 / 2025-07-19 dispensings (outside 12 months). No reversal or compensation rows exist.

[World rows] customers (identity), billing_accounts (payer class for two factors), prescriptions 546f17fd (target) and e8cff9e9 (the other maintenance medication at the same mail-order pharmacy, a selection trap), rx_events (11 on the target: 3 authorizations incl. the earlier replacement, 8 dispensings; 4 on the atorvastatin), appointments (completed 2025-10-20, booked 2026-10-13, no-show 2025-06-10 outside 12 months), telehealth_visits (completed video visit 2026-05-12, virtual near-miss). Removing the billing row sends two factors to baseline; removing the booked visit changes the trim to 21; removing the earlier replacement changes the share to 100. Automatic clauses checked: no prescription passes its expiration, no hold exists (no lapse), the no-show is 14 months back (no attendance action), nothing is in collections.

[Persona] Lorraine Pruitt, a fast-talking school bus dispatcher; volunteers only the theft, being out since Friday and the ask to replace the stolen pills; gives phone for lookup, DOB and MRN for verification (email / SSN last 4 as backups); answers 'only the losartan', 'no police report'; names Kroger Pharmacy #0419 Dublin only after the agent raises a store pharmacy; runs the handed-over move with the values the agent gives; accepts the replacement days and closes. No template labels. Weekdays checked: 2026-08-28 Friday, 2026-08-31 Monday.

[Standard solution / verification] reads 0-6, unlock + user call 7-8 (days_supply 34), unlock + agent call 9-10 (days_supply_per_fill 21). Verification: scratch recompute via check_compute primitives on the handling-time worlds (step 8 on the opening world; step 10 after the move) printed move result 34 with bindings payer 34 / adherence 90 / span 90 / visit 60 (span 182 before the round-2 rework), factor baselines 30,30,30,30, all-baseline 30; replacement result 21 with lost 72, share 85, credit 34, prior 1, missed 0, share 75, trim 7, factor baselines 0,14,47,31,28, all-baseline 34; skip-move replacement 0. Gates: check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK; replay REPLAY OK (23/23 closure); solvability SOLVABILITY OK; grounding GROUNDING OK; cross_fire SCOPE OK; task tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK.

[Visible-context draft recomputation] From the published prose alone: the replacement rule's prerequisite sentence + the lookup showing 'Heartland Mail Order Pharmacy' -> move first; the move rule's four allowances from billing (Medicaid 34), fill ledger (450 -> 90), prescription (1 fill of 90 days ending before expiry -> 90) and appointments (315 days -> 60) -> 34; then the replacement rule step by step -> 72 - 34 = 38, x 75% = 28.5 -> 28, - 7 = 21. Same object, order and values as gold; no second reading found (the video visit is excluded by 'a virtual visit not counting'; the atorvastatin by the customer's statement).

[Revisions] r1: FK fields referral_id / converted_appointment_id seeded as '' were read as dangling -> set to null; replay re-run OK. r2: persona line that asked for the pills to be sent 'where you can pick it up' removed (hint toward the retail prerequisite).

[Round 2 rework, audit audits/policy_task/prescription_renewal_handling]
- F1 / T0-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED): authorization_span_allowance had tiers 'two or more fills -> days // fills' and 'exactly one -> all days', one method at fills = 1. Root cause: the tiers split on the fill count instead of on which method applies. Change: the ladder now splits on whether the fills remaining, at the per-fill supply the prescription carries, would run past expiration: yes -> fit to the authorization (days to expiry // fills, always < the written length); no -> keep the fill length as written (the carried per-fill supply); no fill -> 30. New binding written_fill_days = F('days_supply'). This world: 1 x 90 = 90 <= 182 -> 90 (the fit method would give 182). Result stays MN(34, 90, 90, 60, 90) = 34; the span factor's baseline figure stays 30 (still bears weight); all-baseline 30. Re-run: COMPUTE OK.
- F2 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, latent): the retail fill length could exceed max_days_supply_per_fill. Change: rule adds 'and it never exceeds the largest days' supply per fill of the prescription's class', compute result = MN(four allowances, P('max_days_supply_per_fill')), and rx_fill_authorization joins base_policy_refs. The base clause is now followed, so no overwrite is needed. This world: cap 90, not binding.
- O1: both edges' condition now carries exactly the sentence's state (pharmacy kind only); the days_supply change stays in effect. Propagated to prerequisite_closure.edges[0].condition.
user_scenario: You are Lorraine Pruitt, a 52-year-old school bus dispatcher from Dublin, Ohio, calling the Linden Ridge Patient Services Center on a Monday morning between routes. You talk fast and a little frazzled, but you are polite and you answer exactly what you are asked. Your blood pressure pill, losartan 50 mg tablet, comes to you by mail in a three-month box. The tracking said the new box was delivered to your front porch on Friday, but when you got home it was gone - somebody took it off the porch. You took your last pill from the old bottle on Thursday, so you have been without it since Friday and you are worried. You open with: "Hi, my blood pressure pills got stolen off my porch and I'm completely out - I need you to replace the blood pressure pills that were stolen." You want the replacement set up today, and you are happy for the person on the phone to set it up for you; you do not know how many pills or days you are entitled to and you do not guess. When you are asked who you are, you give your name and that the phone number on your chart is 6145554271. When you are asked to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, March 14, 1974 (1974-03-14), and your medical record number from your visit summary, LR4308816. Only if they still need something else do you give your email, lorraine.pruitt@outlook.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 4417. If they ask which medication was in the box, it was only the losartan; your other pills were not in that package. If they ask about a police report, you reported the missing box to the delivery company but you did not file a police report, so you have no report number. You do not bring up changing pharmacies yourself. Only if the agent tells you the prescription has to be at a store pharmacy, or asks which pharmacy near you it should go to, do you say you would use the Kroger by your house, and you name it exactly as Kroger Pharmacy #0419 Dublin. If the agent says this is something you have to do yourself and hands it to you, you do it right then with exactly the prescription, the pharmacy name and the days' supply the agent tells you, and you read back what it shows. If the agent tells you a number of days for the replacement, you do not argue with it and you accept it. Once the agent tells you the replacement has been authorized, you thank them, say you will head to the pharmacy after your shift, and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.

edges.condition: prescriptions.pharmacy_name names a retail pharmacy rather than a mail-order pharmacy
edges.policy_source: A replacement fill's days' supply is fixed only after the prescription stands at a retail pharmacy rather than at a mail-order pharmacy.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-08-31 the losartan prescription stands at Heartland Mail Order Pharmacy with the mail-order per-fill days' supply of 90; no retail fill length has been recorded.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The patient's move at step 8 sets pharmacy_name = Kroger Pharmacy #0419 Dublin, days_supply = 34 and transfer_count = 1; the replacement's fill_days binding then reads 34 (credit 34) instead of 90.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge (a two-node chain): the move must land before the replacement is computed, because the replacement's credit reads the per-fill days' supply the move records; the reverse order computes the credit on 90 days and writes 0 days, so only one order reproduces the gold terminal state. There are no parallel prerequisites.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the move (step 8) leaves days_supply = 90: credit_days becomes 1 x 90 = 90, (72 - 90) x 75 / 100 truncates to -13, minus 7 is -20, floored at 0 -> days_supply_per_fill 0 instead of 21; the terminal prescriptions row also keeps pharmacy_name Heartland Mail Order Pharmacy, days_supply 90 and transfer_count 0 instead of Kroger Pharmacy #0419 Dublin, 34 and 1 (sens run 2026-09-24).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions moving or changing pharmacies, a retail pharmacy, a per-fill days' supply or any other prerequisite; it says outright that she does not bring up changing pharmacies herself, and names Kroger Pharmacy #0419 Dublin only after the agent says the prescription has to be at a store pharmacy or asks which pharmacy near her it should go to. The move is run by her only when the agent hands it over.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: authorize_replacement_fill_7c6c01e8 reads the prescription only to copy customer_id and raise refills_remaining by one; it never looks at pharmacy_name, days_supply or status and returns its normal receipt whatever pharmacy the prescription stands at. move_prescription_pharmacy_221e1a97 reads transfer_count only to add one and never checks status or pharmacy type.
